### Steps

- Read the web, extension and desktop UI code and the e2e selectors they depend on.
- Rewrote the theme half of public/style.css on the Material 3 Expressive grammar and added a state chip to the player.
- Mirrored the states in the extension toolbar styles and added the playing class in engine.js.

feat(tts): add Kokoro-82M v1.0 as an on-device voice on all three surfaces

Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0, ONNX, fp32) joins Edge, ElevenLabs and Supertonic as
a fourth provider. It runs in-process through onnxruntime-node. Supertonic
reports one duration per clip; Kokoro reports one per phoneme token, so every
word gets a measured timestamp.

Engine
- scripts/fetch-kokoro.mjs (npm run fetch:kokoro) downloads 12 pinned files,
  about 333 MB, into data/kokoro or $KOKORO_DIR: onnx/model.onnx,
  tokenizer.json and nine voices from
  onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX-timestamped at dd4401a9, plus the
  CMUdict-derived dictionary of @met4citizen/headtts@1.3.0 from its npm
  gitHead c08f4ca8 (digest identical in the npm tarball and on GitHub). Same
  guarantees as fetch-supertonic.mjs: a sha256 per file, streaming hash, temp
  file promoted only on a match, re-hash on skip, --force, and a startup
  failure on an unpinned file.
- server/providers/kokoro/ vendors the HeadTTS G2P byte for byte under an MIT
  header, with its LICENSE: dictionary lookup, letter-to-sound fallback,
  Misaki phonemes. No eSpeak and no GPL code.
- server/providers/kokoro.js: a closed voice allowlist checked with
  hasOwnProperty before any path is built; onnxruntime imported on first
  use; one cached session, dictionary, vocabulary and voice table per voice;
  a failed load is retried on the next call. The decoder renders round(d)
  frames of 600 samples per token, and in every probe those rounded frames
  matched the waveform length exactly, so word edges are sample-exact; float
  durations stretched onto the real audio length are the fallback. Pauses
  (punctuation, spaces) stay outside word spans. Words map to char offsets
  in the original text through Intl.Segmenter over the G2P's whitespace
  parts. Input above the 510-token context is cut at the last sentence end
  that fits, else at a word boundary, and the pieces' audio and timings are
  concatenated. Typographic apostrophes become ASCII before G2P, which
  otherwise reads "we're" (curly) as "were" and "I'll" as "ill".
- The vendored number reader round-trips written digits through a double:
  0.00000001 prints as 1e-8 and 309+ digits as Infinity, and its decimal
  branch then recursed until the stack overflowed, failing the chunk on
  every retry. A subclass reads written numbers digit for digit as written
  and leaves all other numbers to the vendored reader. On 6000 generated
  inputs the vendored G2P alone threw on 380 and spoke "undefined" on 127;
  through the provider, 0 and 0.
- Text with nothing to speak (non-Latin script, emoji, punctuation alone)
  plays 300 ms of silence. Pause-only input used to reach the model, which
  ended "..." in an audible burst (RMS 0.100 against 0.080 for words).
- server/lib/words.js gains spansToWords: timed G2P spans to words, with
  unspoken words dropped and wordless speech kept at charStart -1.
- Registered with the on-device latency profile (120 s, no retry on
  timeout); /api/voices lists Kokoro only while its assets are present.

Clients
- The web picker (public/js/main.js) and the extension picker
  (extension/content/engine.js) gain a Kokoro on-device group. sw.js and
  offscreen.js pass provider names through generically, and desktop loads
  the web client, so neither changed.
- The three e2e suites gain self-skipping Kokoro checks that mirror the
  Supertonic ones.

Docs: README (setup, privacy table, limitations, licensing), SECURITY.md
(the pinned-weights control now names fetch-kokoro.mjs and data/kokoro),
tasks/todo.md (Round 11).

B-, bf_emma B-, am_fenrir C+, am_michael C+, am_puck C+, bm_george C,

- model load (InferenceSession.create): 0.63 s with a warm file cache,

- RTF on a 296-char chunk, median of 3: 0.200 (3.83 s for 19.10 s of audio;

- first 8 words of "Kokoro reads this paragraph on your own machine, and

- alignment check on the decoded mp3: median RMS 0.0801 inside word spans,

and Kokoro assets; the baseline was 229 passed, 1 skipped. New: unit tests
for spansToWords, the provider (mocked onnxruntime, the real G2P on a tiny
dictionary: timings, splitting, number reading, silence, load sharing and
retries), the voice allowlist, the registry and the voices route, plus a
live test on the real model.

Known gaps:
- The e2e suites were not run in this change (they bind :3000).
- onnxruntime-node runs inference synchronously on the main thread, so the
  engine answers nothing while a chunk synthesizes (3094 ms of a 3095 ms
  call), and a timed-out chunk keeps running its remaining pieces. Supertonic
  shares this; a worker thread would fix both.
- In the desktop and extension e2e voice switches (Supertonic and Kokoro),
